candidate_result_rows.claim: Measured on the harness of evidence/production_chain/o50_term_forwarding/harness.sh, 47 assertions, all met. Scenario B sends SIGTERM to the WRAPPER PID ONLY -- the form Slurm exercises at the time limit and the one the link-1 boundary showed the old wiring could not survive: the trap fires within 1 s of a 2 s budget; the signal is forwarded to the loop's process group (pgid == the loop's pid, given by `set -m` at the launch); the engine sees it and leaves through its own handler, logging 'Exited cleanly after signal' into BOTH the link log and $BASEDIR/selfplay/stdout.txt; the loop's own TERM trap abandons the cut cycle and exits 143; the wrapper reaps 143 across the interrupted wait; finalize stops the sampler, classifies 'scheduler termination at walltime after 5s (SIGTERM to this wrapper)', leaves .failcount at 0, does not bump .cycles_completed and does NOT cancel the queued successor; and NO SIGKILL is needed. Scenario C, an engine that ignores TERM, escalates to SIGKILL after the grace and completes the whole teardown in 7 s of the 30 s KillWait. Scenarios A, D, E, F and G show the unchanged paths -- clean exit, plain failure, the o33(b) late signal, the storage stop, the pre-flight signal -- behave exactly as before. The o50 closure conditions (i) and (ii) are met; (iii), one real boundary logging the two classification lines, is NOT: Slurm stored link 3's script before this commit, so the earliest link that can carry it is link 4.
assumptions: the harness's stub engine models katago's signal handling (a flag polled between games, then 'Exited cleanly after signal' and status 0); the real engine additionally tears down a CUDA context, which is why the grace is 15 s and not 2
slurmstepd sends SIGTERM to at least the batch script's own process; the fix does not depend on which other processes it also reaches

candidate_result_rows.name: The per-net rows/game record survives retention: 46 complete accepted nets against the 8 the live tree can show, one gap of 13 accepted nets, and no trend is ever fitted across it

working_context.regime: 9x9 production chain BASEDIR runs/p1, read-only; retention KTG_KEEP_SELFPLAY_GENERATIONS=3

candidate_result_rows.claim: The record holds 46 COMPLETE real-net selfplay directories -- 44 recovered from the seven committed versions of rows_per_game.txt plus the two the live tree has since completed -- where the tree itself can only show 8, and where the closing knob check at HEAD could evaluate ZERO tolerances (--trend-nets 9 exceeds the 8 complete directories; and at --trend-nets 3 it aborted on a rows_per_game_random line the pruned table no longer carries). Contiguity is recorded, not guessed: every record carries the predecessor its own observation proves and the accepted-net index from models/, which the pruner never touches. The run's single gap is therefore reported exactly -- t9-s11352064-d2008893 (accepted net 37) -> t9-s15847040-d2653436 (accepted net 51): 13 accepted nets in between have no complete record -- and a window that would span it is REFUSED and narrowed to the contiguous run, loudly, instead of being fitted through. At --marginal-nets 3 --trend-nets 9 --horizon-nets 10 the check now runs end to end and PASSES: marginal r = 16.0361 over 189916 rows / 11843 games, slope -0.0871 rows/game per accepted net over the 8 contiguous records, r_lo = 15.1655, T1 rows_per_cycle 33286.4 (lower90 25843.3) >= 1.2*E = 19200. The record reproduces the validator's boundary numbers on the frozen fixture: 16.9087 = 118361 / 7000.
assumptions: prune_retention.py deletes selfplay generations oldest-first, so what survives in the tree is always a contiguous SUFFIX of the true sequence and the directories listed in ONE observation are consecutive (its candidate list is sp_gens[:len-keep], ordered by mtime, and the shuffle-window `continue` can only skip a suffix of that list)
models/ is never pruned, so its ordering is the accepted-net index
open_obligations: the trend window is 8 of the 9 o48 asks for, because the 13-net gap predates the record and is permanent; it becomes exactly 9 contiguous at the next accepted net (t9-s18522368-d443329 completes when the next net is accepted). Until then every read must report the narrowing, which the check does.

o51 conjunct (iv), one monitoring read demonstrating the slope and r_lo from the record with the live tree holding fewer than 9 complete directories, is met by this acceptance run but is owed again by the launcher at the next scheduled read

At 0: no process is spawned, no directory is created, and a KTG_STAGE_ONLY=1 dry run of the committed loop script stages the same 13 files with the same sha256 as the same dry run of the script at HEAD (the dated directory name normalised away) -- an empty manifest diff. At 1: the archiver hard-links every selfplay/<net>/sgfs/*.sgfs into $BASEDIR/archive/sgf/<net>/, the archived entry is the SAME inode (du -sb delta 0 B over the pass, because du counts an inode once per traversal), a second pass links nothing (linked=0 copied=0 already-linked=2), and the archive still holds the games after its generation is deleted. prune_retention.py protects <basedir>/archive explicitly, and extract_games.snapshot_files reads archive/sgf alongside the live directories and de-duplicates the hard-linked copy (2 files, 1 from the archive, 0 double-counted). codes/data_budget/tests/run_guard_tests.sh still passes 25/25 and check_knobs_9x9 still PASSES with the new knob file.
assumptions: hard links are possible inside one BASEDIR (same filesystem); the archiver falls back to cp -p and says so if not
open_obligations: the human decision on KTG_ARCHIVE_SGF; the flag stays 0 until then

candidate_claim_rows.statement: PROPOSED DISCHARGE, all four conjuncts. (i) codes/eval/rows_history.py + throughput_report.py --history-out append one line per COMPLETE real-net directory -- net, accepted-net index from models/, predecessor, games (sgfs lines), rows (sum of npz binaryInputNCHWPacked.shape[0]), tdata bytes, first and last mtime, link job, recorded_at, source -- to the append-only evidence/production_chain/rows_per_game_history.jsonl, never rewriting a line (idempotent on (net, games, rows)), and a directory becomes a record only when it is no longer the newest. It is written on the read path, before any prune can reach the directory. (ii) codes/eval/seed_rows_history.py seeded it from the seven committed versions of rows_per_game.txt and from the live tree: 46 complete records, and the gap is listed as 't9-s11352064-d2008893 (accepted net 37) -> t9-s15847040-d2653436 (accepted net 51): 13 accepted net(s) in between have no complete record'. NOTE the 13 vs the validator's 12: indices 39..50 are the twelve with no record at all, and index 38, t9-s11651712-d2059673, has one INCOMPLETE observation (908 games, 13.34 rows/game) which is correctly not a complete record. (iii) check_knobs_9x9.py --rows-file accepts the record, and fit_window never fits across a gap: it narrows to the contiguous run ending at the newest record and names the gap that stopped it; with fewer than two contiguous records it refuses outright and substitutes nothing (o41). (iv) demonstrated on a read with the live tree holding 8 complete directories against the 9 asked for: the check runs end to end and PASSES, marginal 16.0361, slope -0.0871 over the 8, r_lo 15.1655. RESIDUAL, carried to the successor obligation: the window is 8 of 9 until the next accepted net.

candidate_claim_rows.statement: Successor to o51's residual and a rider on o48's slope leg. The 13 accepted nets between accepted-net index 37 (t9-s11352064-d2008893) and 51 (t9-s15847040-d2653436) have no complete record and never will: their selfplay directories were deleted by retention passes that ran before any record existed. So o48's nine-net trend window is today NARROWED to the 8 contiguous records ending at t9-s18225024-d381697, and check_knobs_9x9.py says so on every read rather than fitting through the gap. Closes when the contiguous run ending at the newest complete record reaches 9 -- one more accepted net, i.e. as soon as t9-s18522368-d443329 stops being the newest -- and a monitoring read records a nine-record fit with no narrowing note. Until then every read must report both the slope over the narrowed window AND the narrowing itself; a read that reports a nine-net slope without the note is wrong.
